conflicts.fact: Number of lessons remaining after Lesson 1 in the sequence
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the DQB will guide investigation 'over the next 11 lessons' (consistent with 12 total); Lesson 12 evidence parade says 'twelve lessons' of evidence collected, though only 11 precede it. Minor.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the Ohm's Law V-I graph was collected in
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 is the Ohm's Law investigation; Lesson 12 Evidence Parade attributes the V-I graph to Lesson 2, the internal resistance graph to Lesson 7 (it is Lesson 8), and series/parallel readings to Lessons 5-6 (fine).

conflicts.fact: Lesson in which internal resistance graph was collected
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 is the internal resistance investigation; Lesson 12 says Lesson 7 (which is combination circuits).

conflicts.fact: Lesson where P = I²R was derived
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 derives P = IV = I²R = V²/R; Lesson 11 says P = I²R was derived in Lesson 10 (Lesson 10 covers E = Pt) and refers to Lesson 10's model as holding power dissipation.

conflicts.fact: Lesson source of data tables used in Lesson 9
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 says its Lesson 6 data tables were extended with a Power column showing higher-resistance components dissipated more power for the same current; Lesson 6 data were parallel-circuit voltages/currents (6 V battery), not resistance-vs-power data.

conflicts.fact: Cause of the dim lights at power restoration (internal resistance/surge vs low supply voltage)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 and 8 attribute it to internal resistance of the supply and surge current drop Ir; Lesson 11 attributes it to a brownout where supply voltage was below 240 V and lower current; Lesson 10 says 'lower terminal voltage reduced power' during a 'power surge'; Lesson 12 says high effective internal resistance.
Lesson 10 bill: Ksh 12.00 per kWh (lifeline tariff) in the Learned, but its Predict card uses Ksh 20 per unit; Lesson 12 uses approx KES 22 per kWh.
Lesson 9 jiko is 1500 W (Sayona brand); Lesson 10 jiko is 3000 W (and Lesson 11 Sayona is a cooker).

Lesson 10 kettle is 2200 W; Lesson 11 Ramtons kettle draws 9.2 A at 240 V with 26 Ω element (~2200 W, but 240/26 = 9.23 A ok); Lesson 12 kettle is 1,200 W for the Wanjiku house. Different households, minor.
Lesson 7 uses 6 Ω cord feeding appliances; Lesson 9 uses 8 Ω cord carrying 5 A; an 8 Ω cord at 5 A drops 40 V, and Lesson 7's 6 Ω cord is unrealistically large for an extension cord.

Lesson 8 describes a 3 V pack made of two D-cells while Lesson 5 uses 1.5 V AA batteries; Lesson 2 cell 1.5 V terminal voltage drop — no conflict. Lesson 4 previews internal resistance as Lesson 5, but it is taught in Lesson 8.

conflicts.fact: Content of the Lesson 3 cumulative model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 model is a Huruma home circuit with resistor symbols for cord, bulb and kettle; Lesson 4 says the Lesson 3 model showed a battery, wires and a bulb with only bulb resistance labelled.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 6 explanation of neighbour's dim bulb vs. full-voltage claim; Lesson 7 says Lesson 6 'proved' all appliances parallel
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the cord's series resistance only affects that branch; Lesson 7 shows the cord feeding a socket strip so both appliances share the reduced voltage.
